newsitem.title: USA: CSX Norfolk Southern prepare Conrail talks.
newsitem.headline: CSX Norfolk Southern prepare Conrail talks.

text.p: CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. Monday began preparing negotiations on the final division of Conrail Inc., which analysts said they expected would go smoothly and quickly.
Representatives of CSX and Norfolk Southern said the two railroads made preliminary contacts Monday, and a CSX spokesman said the negotiations could start as early as this week.
"We are hoping to conclude the negotiations quickly, in time for a Surface Transportation Board filing by early April," said CSX spokesman Vance Richardson.

Richardson's comments followed Friday's announcement that CSX and Conrail had revised their merger agreement. Under the new deal, CSX is to pay Conrail shareholders $115 per share cash, or about $10.3 billion, and will be allowed to negotiate a division of Conrail with Norfolk Southern.

The announcement set the stage for an end to the five-month takeover battle for Conrail, in which the Philadelphia-based railroad sought, and ultimately failed, to remain intact by preserving its merger with CSX against a hostile bid from Norfolk Southern.

CSX and Norfolk Southern said they would negotiate the breakup of Conrail and a joint purchase of its shares, although the outlines of the breakup are contained in a February 24 proposal by Norfolk Southern that, Norfolk Southern said Friday, had been accepted as the basis for the division.

That proposal sets a roughly 55-45 division of the assets, with CSX getting the larger share, Prudential Securities analyst Brian Routledge said. "I don't think you'll see significant changes," he said.
The proposal also says commonly accepted industry measures should be used in valuing the assets to be divided.

Richardson said CSX aims to close its tender offer for Conrail shares by the initial date set -- April 18 -- although it has the right under the merger agreement to extend that to June 2. "Right now we contemplate completing the tender by April 18," Richardson said.

The Surface Transportation Board is likely to give necessary federal approval for the revised deal because it will offer two strong competitors in a region formerly dominated by Conrail, said PNC Bank analyst Charles Vincent.
"I'm pretty sure that this is going to make it a lot easier to get it (the deal) through the Surface Transportation Board," he said.
Richardson said the federal agency already had been notified.
Conrail will not participate in the discussions on its breakup, CSX said.
While the negotiations are under way, "We're going to be operating a railroad," Conrail spokesman Bob Libkind said.

Philadelphia mayor Ed Rendell on Monday told reporters he hoped to use private meetings with the companies and "leverage" with the transportation board in a campaign to protect jobs of Conrail employees.

"I intend to meet with all of the principals, but I intend to meet with them privately," Rendell said. "We will push our cause and we have a great deal of leverage with the Surface Transportation Board."
